stories.headline: Lakers' Luka Doncic has altercation with fan after NBA Cup loss to Spurs
stories.summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic was shoved by a fan following Friday's loss to the Spurs in a brief altercation that he chalked up as a postgame ritual gone awry.
stories.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic had a brief altercation with a fan in the aftermath of Friday night's 99-96 loss to the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center.

Doncic, 27, chalked up the situation as a postgame ritual gone awry.

"I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game," Doncic said. "Then, I heard he didn't want it, so I went back to grab it. He just pushed me. Then, I gave it to somebody else."

The altercation took place as Doncic walked off the floor and headed toward the visitors' locker room just minutes after the Lakers were eliminated from the NBA Cup, becoming the first team this season to squander multiple 20-point leads.

Video from Amazon Prime's postgame broadcast showed Doncic walking past a man and a woman sitting courtside and throwing a white wristband in their direction.

The woman appeared to say something to Doncic just before he tossed the wristband. But just as quickly, Doncic turned back around to retrieve it. The man next to the woman picked the wristband up and handed it to Doncic, before shoving him as he turned to walk back toward the visitors' locker room.

The shove jolted Doncic somewhat and teammate Jarred Vanderbilt stepped in to intervene along with members of Frost Bank Center security. The man was subsequently ejected.

"I just heard somebody say they didn't want it," Doncic said. "I went back to get it, and then he pushed me. I just gave the wristband to somebody else."

It's unclear whether Doncic will face any discipline from the NBA.

Los Angeles led Friday's contest by 20 points in the second quarter and by 16 at intermission before San Antonio outscored the Lakers 30-14 in the third quarter. Reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year Keldon Johnson tied the score at 68-all with 1.8 seconds left in the frame with a 23-foot corner 3-pointer. The Spurs got a combined 17 points from Stephon Castle (9 points) and Victor Wembanyama (8 points) in the fourth quarter to pull out the win.

Doncic scored a game-high 31 points on 31 attempts for his 12th 30-point game of the season, tying two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the most in the NBA.

"The reality is, that's the barometer in the West right now, and this was a great test for us," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "We'll get better from it. They're disappointed right now and it's a natural emotion from losing a game. I told them this morning, 'We're going to get feedback [from the game]. And when we wake up tomorrow, if we've won the game or lost, we're still a good team on Saturday morning.'"

ESPN Research contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Bo Nix, after one of his worst games for Broncos, says 'I let the team down'
stories.summary: After one of the most difficult starts of his NFL career, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said "I let the team down'' in a 27-5 loss to the Steelers on Friday.
stories.body:
PITTSBURGH -- After one of the most difficult starts of his NFL career, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said "I let the team down'' in a 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday.

The Broncos' first Black Friday game certainly won't go in Nix's scrapbook -- or the offense's -- as the Broncos mustered just 205 net yards, as Nix's lone fumble was recovered for a touchdown and one of his two interceptions returned for a touchdown.

"It's frustrating for sure, and I let the team down,'' Nix said. "[That is] the last thing I want to do as a quarterback, as a leader of the team. ... [My teammates] didn't let me get too down. I was wanting to get a little more down than they were letting me.''

In a game played in a steady rain with a wind chill of 29 degrees at kickoff, Nix finished 22-of-49 passing for 169 yards and was sacked three times, with the three turnovers. It was the first time in Nix's 47 career starts, including regular season and playoffs, that he had three turnovers and was sacked three times in the same game.

The struggles in the rain were reminiscent of a 10-9 win over the Jets in 2024, his rookie year; Nix finished with a career-low 60 yards passing at a rain-swept MetLife Stadium.

The Broncos' 204 net yards Friday were their third fewest this season, trailing the 176 net yards in the season-opening loss at Kansas City and 168 in a Week 6 win over Seattle.

Broncos coach Sean Payton was quick to defend Nix, pointing the finger more at his playcalls that led to the first-half turnovers.

"Starts with me,'' Payton said. "Early on, we gave them opportunities with momentum, and that falls on me.''

Nix and Payton circled the QB's first-quarter fumble as one of those opportunities for the Steelers. The Steelers came into Friday's game after benching -- and eventually waiving -- quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who took aim at Steelers coach Mike McCarthy in an interview on "The Pat McAfee Show."

But in a scoreless game, with the Broncos' offense already sputtering, Denver faced a third-and-15 from its own 19-yard line. After the snap, the Broncos tried to set up a screen pass to running back Tyler Badie, but the Steelers had multiple defenders quickly beat blocks, and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton promptly dropped to get in the passing lane in front of Badie.

As Nix tried to reset after he saw Badie covered, he lost the ball, and T.J. Watt recovered it in the end zone. The touchdown brought the Steelers' crowd into full-throated support that never dissipated.

"Going down 7-0, with a fumble recovered for a touchdown is definitely not ideal,'' Nix said. "That started us off on the wrong foot, and we could never get out of the hole. ... Momentum is a real thing.''

"I'm kicking myself for the first score,'' Payton said. "You know, we're running a screen play, but it's a slower-developing screen play, and coming out [from near the end zone], that's not too good. ... This is one of those games, 10 points [Friday] is different than 10 points on any normal -- 10 points is a lot -- so a seven-point swing, they score on defense, that's why I kick myself relative to a few of those calls.''

It didn't get much better for Nix or the offense the rest of the way. With 1:44 left in the first half, on a first-and-10 from the Broncos' 28-yard line, Nix tried to fit a ball to Jaylen Waddle up the right sideline.

But Nix was short on the throw, and Jalen Ramsey returned the interception 36 yards for a touchdown that gave the Steelers a 24-5 lead.

"I saw [Ramsey], I just didn't throw it high enough over his head,'' Nix said. "Once they got 14-0 momentum, it's tough, that's not what you want to do on the road against a good team. A good team is not going to let you back in.''

Nix threw his second interception in the fourth quarter with just under nine minutes left.

The loss means the Broncos (8-3) lost a chance to move a game in front of the Kansas City Chiefs (8-3) in the AFC West and puts Denver two games behind the Buffalo Bills (10-1) in the quest for home-field advantage. The Broncos face the Bills on Christmas in Denver.

stories.headline: Source: Cubs agree to terms with Japanese pitcher Hiromi Itoh
stories.summary: The Cubs continued a busy month by agreeing to terms with Japanese right-hander Hiromi Itoh on Friday night, a source told ESPN on Friday, confirming a report by FanSided.
stories.body:
The Chicago Cubs continued a busy month by agreeing to terms with Japanese right-hander Hiromi Itoh on Friday night, a source confirmed to ESPN, adding him alongside countryman Teruaki Sato and plugging Itoh into a needy rotation.

Itoh, 29, joins the Cubs four days after they signed left-handed starter Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract and three days after adding Sato, who is expected to play right field, on a six-year, $120 million deal. Both those agreements became official Friday.

Terms of Itoh's deal have not been disclosed.

During his six seasons with Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters in Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball, Itoh led the league in innings pitched (1,000⅔) and strikeouts (902), made at least 23 starts each season and won the Sawamura Award -- NPB's version of the Cy Young Award -- in 2025.

This past season, the right-hander was 10-10 with a 3.18 ERA and 159 strikeouts over 172⅔ innings while walking just 4.7% of batters faced.

Itoh was a first-round pick by Hokkaido in the 2020 NPB draft, and he has had an ERA above 3.00 in just two of his six seasons. He led the Pacific League with 14 wins in 2024 and was dominant in 2025 with a league-best 196⅔ innings and 195 strikeouts while finishing second among qualified pitchers in walk rate at 3.6%.

Some scouts have questioned his overall impact in MLB because his fastball velocity is below average, sitting 90-94 mph, and he doesn't have a plus secondary pitch to rack up strikeouts, relying most on a good slider and splitter from his six-pitch mix. What is not in doubt is his durability and control.

Itoh contributed to Japan's gold medal run at the 2021 Olympics, pitching five scoreless innings in three games, and he also pitched for his country in the 2026 World Baseball Classic.

The Cubs went into the offseason desperately needing rotation help, with Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes all becoming free agents, and Ben Brown and Cade Horton coming off surgery. Rogers and Itoh join Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera and Braxton Garrett.

With Itoh, Sato and Kaima Taira (Toronto Blue Jays) all signing, the three big NPB stars have come off the board before the anticipated Dec. 1 lockout. Japanese players have a 45-day posting window, but the CBA's expiration date of Dec. 1 truncated it by about a third.

FanSided was first to report Itoh's agreement with the Cubs.

ESPN's Kiley McDaniel contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Kakko scores twice in 3rd as Kraken hand Oilers their 5th straight loss
stories.summary: — Kaapo Kakko scored twice in a two-minute span in the third period and the Seattle Kraken beat Edmonton 4-2 on Friday night, handing the Oilers their fifth straight loss in the opener the home-and-home set.
stories.body:
EDMONTON, Alberta -- — Kaapo Kakko scored twice in a two-minute span in the third period and the Seattle Kraken beat Edmonton 4-2 on Friday night, handing the Oilers their fifth straight loss in the opener the home-and-home set.


The teams will meet again Saturday night in Seattle.


Jordan Eberle and Vince Dunn also scored and Matty Beniers had two assists for the Kraken (12-10-1). They have won two of their last three and snapped an eight-game road skid against the Oilers.


Philipp Grubauer made 16 stops before suffering an upper-body injury and being replaced by Joey Daccord, who made nine saves.


Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl scored for the skidding Oilers (17-7-4). Edmonton went 1 for 8 on the power play.


McDavid extended his season-opening home points streak to 14 games and became the sixth player in NHL history to reach 60 points in 28 games or fewer — the first since Mario Lemieux did so in 1995-96 in 21 contests. The other ones to hit 60 this early were Wayne Gretzky, Bernie Nicholls, Mike Bossy and Phil Esposito.


Tristan Jarry made 27 saves for Edmonton.


------

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 49
Goals: 41
Assists: 19

Nov. 27: Columbus Crew 1-0 Inter Miami

That's a wrap on 2026 for Mr. Messi. After conceding in the second minute of second-half stoppage time, the Herons' season is over, eliminated just two games into their postseason campaign.

Miami was held scoreless in both Round 1 contests against the Crew, and with Messi also being held off the score sheet on Decision Day, it's actually been 26 days since the World Cup winner registered a direct goal contribution.

Now the 39-year-old has a couple of months to rest up before the 2027 sprint season kicks off in February.

Nov. 21: Inter Miami 0-3 Columbus Crew
Ouch. That one hurt.

Miami and Messi are staring down the barrel of an early exit from the MLS playoffs after slumping to a 3-0 home loss to the Columbus Crew in Game 1 of their first-round series on Saturday.

The Argentine magician drew a blank as the Crew ran riot with a brace for Gonzalo Tapia either side of a goal from Taha Habroune.

Miami must now win when the best-of-three game series heads to Columbus for Game 2 on Friday to force a decisive Game 3 back in Miami on Dec. 2.

Nov. 7: Inter Miami 3-3 Charlotte FC
Although neither team had much at stake on Decision Day, Miami and Charlotte offered up an entertaining 3-3 draw at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

The Herons leapt out to a three-goal lead thanks to Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul -- with Messi, in a rare occurrence, not assisting any -- but were pegged back by the visitors to ensure both teams shared the points.

With the regular season now wrapped up, Miami's second-place finish in the East means Messi and Co. will face-off with the Columbus Crew in the first round of the postseason.

Nov. 1: New England Revolution 1-2 Inter Miami

Messi once again provided the magic touch for Miami, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Herons' marquee star set up a goal and scored the winner as Miami leapfrogged New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

After going behind to a Dániel Gazdag goal, Miami responded with a strike from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- before the 39-year-old scored the winner in the 83rd minute. Sumptuous stuff.

Oct. 28: FC Cincinnati 2-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists for Messi in what was an eventful 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

Luis Suárez scored in the 61st minute to give Miami a 1-0 lead, and then the reigning MLS Cup champions needed some late-game heroics to salvage a point. They still fell to third in the Eastern Conference, after New England beat Red Bull New York 3-2 on Wednesday.

Oct. 24: Red Bull New York 2-0 Inter Miami
It has been an eventful few days for Messi. Just a day before the match, he traveled to Spain to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first individual soccer player to earn the honor.

He then returned to the United States and joined his teammates in New Jersey, starting on the bench before coming on in the 56th minute. However, he was unable to make an impact as the hosts secured a 2-0 victory, ending Miami's three-game winning streak.

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Chelsea, Tottenham eye move for Wolfsburg's Kumbedi
stories.summary: Both Chelsea and Tottenham are reportedly looking at Wolfsburg's Saël Kumbedi as a possible new signing. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are set to battle it out for France right back Saël Kumbedi, while Manchester United are interested in Como's Nico Paz as a replacement for Bruno Fernandes. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea and Tottenham could battle it out for the signing of Wolfsburg right back Saël Kumbedi, reports TEAMtalk. The 21-year-old has been an emerging talent for the 2. Bundesliga side, with that form being recognized in his recent outings for the senior France national team. Kumbedi has a contract until 2029, and while that interest from Chelsea and Tottenham is there, interest is also present from Fulham and Manchester City.

- Como star Nico Paz is against the idea of returning to Real Madrid but is open to the idea of joining Manchester United, reports The Athletic. Paz, 22, has again been one of Europe's standout young players this season and is seen by Argentina as an heir to Lionel Messi for the national side. Paz joined Como from Madrid in August 2024, and the Spanish club has a clause that they can re-sign him for €80 million this summer. However, without any assurances of a prominent role, Paz would rather go elsewhere. Those other options would include United, who might need to replace Bruno Fernandes in the near future, albeit the club are unlikely to be his first choice.

- Paris Saint-Germain have made enquiries to Atlético Madrid about the availability of Julián Álvarez this January, with a winter deal being eyed. That's according to TEAMTalk, which claims that the Parisiens are showing interest in the Argentina forward, alerting fellow suitors Arsenal. However, it seems as though Atlético are not considering an exit midseason, with the 25-year-old firmly back in the first-team picture after the fallout from a failed attempt to join Barcelona in the summer.

- Arsenal, Liverpool, and Manchester United are considering a move for Borussia Dortmund defender Kouakou Gadou, claims German newspaper BILD. The 19-year-old French center back joined the Bundesliga club from RB Salzburg in the summer, and has quickly become a regular for the side. That has alerted many clubs to his quality, but Dortmund seemingly won't allow an exit for anything under €80 million, ahead of the winter market.

- Chelsea won't consider a January transfer exit for Marco Palestra, despite links surrounding a move for the defender. That's according to transfer journalist Nicolo Schira, who claims that the 21-year-old is untouchable, despite making just two starts since joining the Blues from Atalanta in the summer. The Italy international has a contract until 2033, suggesting a long-term future for the right back.

Other rumors
- Barcelona are set for fresh talks with forward Fermin Lopez over a new contract to block interest from Arsenal, Chelsea, and Manchester United in the 23-year-old. (TeamTalk)

- Valencia have submitted an offer to sign Alexander Sørloth from Atletico Madrid, with the 30-year-old striker also being tracked by Juventus ahead of the winter market. (Ekrem Konur)

- Mateo Kovacic is attracting attention from clubs ahead of the January transfer window, with Nassr, Juventus, and AC Milan among those following the midfielder. The 32-year-old has a contract with Manchester City that expires in the summer. (Ekrem Konur)

- Former PSG and Chelsea defender Thiago Silva is closing in on another contract with Fluminense that will see the 42-year-old stay on until December 2027. (Nicolo Schira)

- Alex Meret is facing an uncertain future with Napoli, with contract talks stalling between the goalkeeper and club. (Nicolo Schira)

- Marseille could sanction an exit for Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg in January, with Juventus and Fiorentina tracking the midfielder. If the 31-year-old stays, then an exit clause becomes available in the summer, worth €2 million. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Manchester United continue to closely monitor Sporting CP star Maxi Araújo, having scouted the left back in the recent Champions League encounter between the teams. The Uruguayan international has an €80 million clause in his contract that could allow for a permanent deal, but Sporting CP could accept an offer worth roughly €50 million to €60 million. (SportWitness)

stories.headline: Qatar Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli quickest in disrupted second practice
stories.summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli topped back-to-back practice sessions Friday at the Qatar Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli topped back-to-back practice sessions Friday at the Qatar Grand Prix.

New world champion Antonelli carried his form into second practice to go fastest in a disrupted session that finished under the Virtual Safety Car.

Antonelli's teammate George Russell crossed the line 0.127 seconds adrift in second place, with McLaren's Lando Norris third-fastest.

Norris' teammate Oscar Piastri was fourth, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen rounding out the top five.

Lewis Hamilton stopped on track in the final stages after reporting on his Ferrari team radio that he was having issues with his engine and finished eighth.

He said: "Something's happened. I've lost power. I've lost the engine."

Isack Hadjar in the other Red Bull was sixth-fastest, with Charles Leclerc behind in seventh.

Early in the session, Leclerc ended up spinning off and returned to the Ferrari garage to have his car checked.

The session was stopped due to gravel on the track, leaving the cars to return to the pit -- and the red flag impacted Russell, who had been on a fast lap.

Not long after the action resumed, a red flag was waved when Pierre Gasly skidded off the track on Turn 14 and went into the gravel, with a piece of polystyrene also stuck to the front of his Alpine.

The session was extended by 13 minutes and Hamilton and Verstappen came almost wheel-to-wheel, but an FIA review deemed no further investigation for driving erratically.

- Qatar GP organizers keen to show world 'real situation' amid safety concerns

- George Russell breaks silence on Max Verstappen criticism: 'Amusing'

- Qatar Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli leads George Russell in first practice

Hamilton's session was ended after losing power, and he parked the car on the side of the track, leading to a Virtual Safety Car being deployed in the final minutes.

Antonelli was crowned Formula 1's youngest champion earlier this month with four rounds remaining and the season is set to conclude in Abu Dhabi next week.

The Italian had already impressed on Friday after finishing top in the first practice session and believes it had been a "productive day" for his team.

"I think it's going to be very close between me and George, then of course you can never write off Max and the others," Antonelli said, in quotes reported on the official F1 website.

"There's been already weekends where we were very strong in the beginning, then in qualifying the others seem to make a big step and get close. We just need to keep working, keep improving and then we'll try to be ready for tomorrow.

"I think [it] was a productive day. I think we tried a lot of things on the car, also between FP1 and FP2.

"FP2 seems like we did a step back with the car but [it] was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes and it's not easy.

"Long run, the front left is the one that is dropping, just need to find the right balance for qualifying and then the race."

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: José Mourinho hails Jude Bellingham but refuses Zinedine Zidane comparison
stories.summary: José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
stories.body:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.

Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, continuing his superb start to the season.

The midfielder's form has helped Madrid keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the LaLiga table, with a three-point gap between the pair going into this weekend's games.

"I don't like to compare players from different generations," Mourinho said in a news conference on Friday when asked to rank Bellingham with Zidane.

"Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare."

Mourinho rested Bellingham for the first half against PSV, only to see his team struggle and go 1-0 down -- and the coach responded by sending on Bellingham at halftime to turn the match around.

Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé are two of the Madrid players who have featured most in LaLiga this season, with 1047 and 1163 minutes respectively.

"The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule," Mourinho said. "It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude."

- Jude Bellingham: I don't care about the Ballon d'Or

- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'

The victory over PSV left Madrid top of the Champions League table on 15 points from five games, but Mourinho wouldn't accept that his side are now among the favourites to win the competition. "It's very early," Mourinho said. "We don't know how the teams will arrive at the key moment, the knockout. Right now the only thing I want is not to play the playoffs.

Mourinho said Trent Alexander-Arnold was unavailable to face Alavés on Saturday with illness, while he insisted that he doesn't want to add to his squad in the January window.

"I don't want anyone to come in, or anyone to leave," Mourinho said. "The door is closed in both ways... I don't want to see news about the market, because I don't want anyone."

stories.headline: Friday Night Lights,' 'Ted Lasso' top poll ranking 21st-century sports shows
stories.summary: A Seton Hall poll crowns America's favorite modern fictional sports TV series.﻿
stories.body:
It's been quite the year for scripted sports series, with milestones worth celebrating and new chapters worthy of clearing space on the couch.

"Friday Night Lights" hit its two-decade anniversary. "One Tree Hill" turned 23 -- a number Nathan Scott and Michael Jordan would both approve of. On the more modern side, "Ted Lasso" returned for its fourth season, while "All American" wrapped up its Season 8 series finale.

Through different eras and sports, fans have plenty of reasons to get invested, so we tapped Seton Hall for a poll on America's favorite sports show of the 21st century.

"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" took the top spots among the general population at 16% and 15%, respectively. The Texas-based football drama also held the edge among avid sports fans, 25% to 22%, and casual sports fans, 23% to 18%.

"The two leaders in the clubhouse for top series indicate that depth and consistency resonate the most with all sports fans," said Len DeLuca, associate director, Seton Hall Sports Poll and instructor in the Seton Hall Stillman Center for sport management. "'Friday Night Lights' was on NBC 14 years before 'Ted Lasso' premiered on Apple TV. This proves that sports content is agnostic to platform."

Whether your loyalty lies with the Dillon Panthers, the Tree Hill Ravens or AFC Richmond, there's a good chance your favorite fictional team has put you through highs and lows. And much like rooting for a real team, picking a favorite show can inspire a spirited debate.

Here are the key findings.

Football leads a multisport lineup
Among the general population, "Friday Night Lights" led all shows at 16%, with "All American" at 10%, "The Game" at 8% and "Ballers" at 7%. That gave football four of the eight highest-polling series overall. Viewers had plenty of interest in the drama surrounding the game, from high school rivalries to the business of professional sports.

Still, football didn't sweep the podium: Soccer's "Ted Lasso" and karate's "Cobra Kai" finished second and third at 15% and 13%, respectively. With 12%, "A League of Their Own" added representation for baseball and took the fourth spot. Hockey's "The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers" and basketball's "One Tree Hill" also drew 7% each, matching "Ballers."

The generation gap
The age ranges didn't differ entirely, but different generations tended to root for different fictional teams.

18-34: "Ted Lasso" led with 17%, followed by "All American," "The Game" and "The English Game" at 14% each. Newer titles also found an audience here: "Heated Rivalry" drew 10%, its strongest showing across the age groups.

35-54: This group showed the most love for "Cobra Kai," which topped its list at 19%. "Friday Night Lights" followed at 18%, with "Ted Lasso" at 15%. "One Tree Hill" and "Eastbound & Down" also had their strongest showings here at 10% each.

55+: "Friday Night Lights" took the lead at 17%, narrowly ahead of "A League of Their Own" at 16%. "Ted Lasso" rounded out the top three at 13%. The drop-off was sharper for teen dramas such as "All American" and "One Tree Hill," which drew 5% and 3%, respectively.

Commonalities and contrasts between sports fans and nonfans
Sports fans and nonfans found some common ground, even if they weren't watching the same shows. "Friday Night Lights" led among sports fans at 23%, followed by "Ted Lasso" at 19% and "Cobra Kai" and "A League of Their Own" at 16% each.

Among nonfans, "Cobra Kai" moved into first at 8%, with "Ted Lasso" and "A League of Their Own" tied at 7%. Coach Eric Taylor (played by Kyle Chandler) had a tougher time with that crowd, as "Friday Night Lights" drew 5%.

The biggest divide, though, was in those who selected "don't know/no opinion": 69% of nonfans compared with 28% of sports fans. The crossover appeal is there, but viewers with less interest in sports need more motivation to tune in.

The men's and women's lineups look a little different
"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" finished first and second among both men and women, but the order differs after that. Among men, "Cobra Kai" took third at 15%, followed by "A League of Their Own" at 11%.

Women flipped those two, with "A League of Their Own" drawing 14% and "Cobra Kai" at 11%. "Make It or Break It" and "Heated Rivalry" also drew higher percentages among women than men, both at 6% to 4%.

New shows are earning their stripes
Some newer series are already finding a place alongside the familiar favorites. "Chad Powers" drew 6% overall, followed by "Heated Rivalry" at 5% and "Running Point" and "Off Campus" at 4% each.

For avid sports fans, "Chad Powers" reached 13%, matching "The Game" in that group. "Heated Rivalry," meanwhile, had its strongest showing among adults ages 18-34 at 10%. The established shows have a head start, but the newcomers are getting some playing time.

Editor's Note: These results are derived from a Seton Hall Sports Poll conducted Oct. 8 to Oct. 13, 2026, among 1,632 adults. The Poll, which is sponsored by The Sharkey Institute within Seton Hall University's Stillman School of Business, features a national representative sample from YouGov Plc., weighted on U.S. Census Bureau figures for age, gender, ethnicity, education, income and geography with a margin of error of +/- 3.0 percent.

stories.headline: 'Can't judge them': who Papenhuyzen wants at the Storm
stories.summary: Ex-Melbourne star Ryan Papenhuyzen has made some big calls on who should be the next Storm coach and the one to keep from Cameron Munster and Harry Grant.
stories.body:
Ryan Papenhuyzen empathises with Cameron Munster but believes Melbourne must prioritise keeping Harry Grant if the NRL powerhouse can't hold on to both superstars.

Munster on Tuesday rejected an offer from the Storm believed to be for one year with the option of another season, labelling the terms "disappointing".

The Storm are also fighting to keep Grant, and Papenhuyzen was unequivocal when asked on Wednesday who the club should target if salary-cap pressures meant only one of the newly crowned Australian World Cup winners could stay.

"I went through something similar as Munster where I thought the club had low-balled me," the happily retired 2020 premiership-winning hero told AAP.

"But having my time out of the game now, they've got their reasons for offering those certain amounts and it might not be enough (for Munster).

"Penrith have done it for years and years. They get to a point where they can't hold their players and they've got a price for their players.

"So I understand Munster's perspective. He wants to earn as much as he can in his career and he wants to win a premiership, so that probably limits his opportunities.

"If a club's got money and they're in a premiership window, it's probably a good chance he'll go to that club."

At 28, skipper Grant is four years younger than Munster and more important long-term to the Storm, Papenhuyzen believes.

"Harry's done a brilliant job in terms of leadership," the ex-Clive Churchill Medallist turned caddy said after playing in the Australian PGA Championship pro-am in Sydney.

"The amount of care he has for everyone in that group and the way he thinks about the game, I feel really sorry for him over the last 12 months (when Melbourne missed the finals) because he's always trying to find new ideas to bring everyone.

"He's a great leader for that club going forward. I'd hate to see him go because he's a player you want to build a club around and I guess Munster is towards the back end of his career.

"He had a great World Cup, but World Cups are different to NRL seasons. You've got to lock in for a month with that, and an NRL season's a long time."

Pressed on who he'd keep as a priority, Papenhuyzen said: "Harry's probably the one leadership-wise. Just his qualities are really admirable.

"You know what Munster brings to the game. He gives you confidence standing next to him, knowing what he's going do, but I just think Harry ..."

With coach Craig Bellamy confirming he is moving on at the end of 2027, Papenhuyzen also suspects Grant might be a better for the Storm's new mentor, whomever that may be.

"Harry's really respected and in terms of trying to keep the culture, he's very open-minded too," the BMW golf correspondent said.

"He's open to new ideas, whereas Munster is very much like Bellamy - he's sort of got his way and it's worked for him for so long.

"Whatever they both decide to do, you can't judge them. It's never a right or wrong decision."

Papenhuyzen believes it would be "awesome" if Billy Slater succeeded Bellamy, but suspects "life is too good" for the Storm legend to be a head NRL coach.

"I love Jyles. If he went back there, I'd be awfully encouraged of how well they're going to go. They'd probably be my two."

But Papenhuyzen, also open to helping out the new coach, nominated Bellamy's son Aaron as a left-field option.

"Aaron's awesome with people," he said.

"He's awesome with the wider playing group and he understands that Craig sometimes pushes the boundaries. Aaron's a bit more like Wendy - Craig's, Craig's wife.

"They're both a bit more more gentle, so you've got that loving, nurturing side and potentially (he could do the job).

"I do know you just need people around you. We'd be silly to say the coach controls everything."
